title: AI Firms Build Phones for 100B Parameter Models by 2028
summary:
Qualcomm is witnessing a shift in the smartphone market as its partners in the artificial intelligence sector begin to manufacture their own handheld hardware. CEO Cristiano Amon disclosed that leading AI firms are targeting the ability to run 100B parameter models continuously on a device by 2028. While Amon declined to identify the companies, he confirmed that several entities at the forefront of the industry are already building these phones to enable constant on-device processing.

The remarks were made during the Snapdragon Summit in Hawaii, where Amon also predicted that smart glasses will become the dominant category of AI wearables. To challenge the software lock-in created by Nvidia's CUDA, Qualcomm recently acquired Modular. The drive for 100B parameter on-device capabilities suggests a move toward greater vertical integration among AI developers seeking to control the hardware hosting their models.

selectedTweets.text:
Qualcomm CEO reveals AI companies want phones running 100-billion-parameter models continuously by 2028--and confirms some are building phones

Cristiano Amon: “I have to be careful not to disclose names, but some AI companies—some of the companies at the forefront of AI—are telling Qualcomm, ‘By 2028, I need to make sure that I have the ability to run at least a 100-billion-parameter model in a phone, and I need to have this thing running kind of all the time.’”

Alex Heath: “So you’re saying there are AI companies that are talking about—”

Cristiano Amon: “Well, AI companies are starting to do phones.”

Qualcomm’s CEO on the coming AI phone supercycle

@cristianoamon on the China vs. US AI sentiment, how AI is changing smartphones and wearables, Qualcomm’s data center strategy, and 6G.

We discuss why he thinks phones aren’t going away, how agents will use our personal context, and why he expects smart glasses to become the biggest category of AI wearables. We also cover differences in consumer AI adoption between China and the US, Qualcomm’s acquisition of Modular to offer developers an alternative to Nvidia’s software, and what 6G could change about the devices we use.

This conversation was recorded live at Qualcomm’s recent Snapdragon Summit in Hawaii.
